51421889.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to human GLS1 expressed in Escherichia coli strain BL21 (DE3) by ITC analysis

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - ITC Assay: ITC (MicroCal iTC200) was used to determine the binding affinities between GLS1 and the synthesized compounds. Proteins with a concentration of 50 μM were prepared in the assay buffer (20 mM Tris-HCl and 150 mM NaCl, pH = 7.4) and subsequently injected into titration cells, and compounds with a concentration of 300 μM in the same assay buffer were loaded in syringes. The whole injection procedure was set with intervals of 180 s and a stirring speed of 1000 rpm, involving 19 injections in total. In order to prevent interference and ensure the accuracy, the first titration of the ligand solution was 0.5 μL. Origin software was finally used to analyze the data obtained to determine the binding parameters, including the enthalpy value (ΔH), the entropy value (ΔS), and the association constant (Ka = 1/Kd).
original_paragraph.Figure 3 caption: Figure 3. Compound 13b (LL202) directly bound to GLS1. (A) Thermal stability of GLS1 treated with different concentrations of 13b, determined by a standard PTS assay. ΔTm values were obtained from the mean values of three independent assays. (B) SPR-based binding assay of 13b with GLS1. (C) Chemical structure of 13b.
original_paragraph.Supporting Information: Supporting Information is available free of charge at https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/acs.jmedchem.0c02044. Figures of iterative structural modifications, glutamine saturation profiles, Lineweaver–Burk plots, kinetic constants, derivatives of the protein melting curves, thermal shift vs GLS1 enzyme pIC50 plot, HCT116 and MDA-MB-436 cell proliferation pIC50 vs GLS1 enzyme pIC50 plots, SPR-based binding assays, direct binding experiments, intracellular metabolite levels, 1H and 13C NMR spectra, HRMS spectra, and HPLC spectra (PDF) Molecular formula strings (CSV)
